The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({e}^{x}-{x}^{2}-2)^{′}={e}^{x}-2x
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}_{n}^{x}-{x}_{n}^{2}-2}{{e}_{n}^{x}-2{x}_{n}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}_{0}^{x}-{x}_{0}^{2}-2}{{e}_{0}^{x}-2{x}_{0}} \\  & =1.4-\frac{{e}^{1.4}-{1.4}^{2}-2}{{e}^{1.4}-2\cdot 1.4} \\  & =1.4-0.075\,844… \\  & =1.324\,155….\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{{e}_{1}^{x}-{x}_{1}^{2}-2}{{e}_{1}^{x}-2{x}_{1}} \\  & =(1.324\,155…)-\frac{{e}^{1.324\,155…}-(1.324\,155…)^{2}-2}{{e}^{1.324\,155…}-2\cdot (1.324\,155…)} \\  & ≈1.319,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
